{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./SpTrSv_Final.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --nodes=1            -> -N 1
#   --ntasks-per-node=64 -> -n 64
#   -t 6:00:00           -> -t 6h
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 64 -t 6h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name="SpTrSv_Final" not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --output/--error use %j expansion (jobid) which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filenames may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  # NOTE: Slurm --export=ALL not translated.
  # Performance implication: usually none (Flux typically inherits the environment), but if your site sanitizes environments, missing exports could change runtime behavior.

  source init_var.sh
  export OMP_NUM_THREADS=64
  export MKL_NUM_THREADS=64

  SOURCE_DIR=$(pwd)
  echo "Start SpTrSv Final"

  cd "${SOURCE_DIR}/build/example" || exit 1
  rm -rf SpTrSv_Final_20.csv

  for sparse_mat in matrix/*.mtx; do
      echo "Processing ${sparse_mat}"
      flux run -n 64 ./SpTrSv_Final "${sparse_mat}"
  done
fi
"
}
